lines.trans: Oh my goodness, what is this—scissors? What is he doing to my baby right now?
If you want this handbag to stay unharmed, get inside the house within thirty minutes.
If you fail to arrive in time, even I cannot guarantee what I might do to this little one.
Out of all of them, he picked an expensive baby! You petty jerk—just dare lay a finger on it!
Where is my handbag?
I was sorry about earlier.
Save it—just hand over my bag right now!
I was sorry earlier and I am sorry for lying to you last time too—I am apologizing right here.
Hey, are you a grade-schooler? That is so childish I cannot even laugh.
Anyway, stop talking about moving out and just stay right here until your apartment move-in day.

meanings.note: Used as numeral + counter (30분).

examples.text: 이 가방이 무사하길 바란다면 30분 내로 집에 들어와라.
examples.trans: If you want this handbag to stay unharmed, get inside the house within thirty minutes.
This point about thirty minutes is really important.

meanings.note: Used as noun + subject (가방이).

examples.text: 이 가방이 무사하길 바란다면 30분 내로 집에 들어와라.
examples.trans: If you want this handbag to stay unharmed, get inside the house within thirty minutes.
Where is my handbag?

examples.text: 저 가위 낼게요. 안 내면 진 거, 가위바위보!
examples.trans: I am going to throw scissors. Lose if you don't throw—rock, paper, scissors!
The topic of scissors came up during this shoot.

examples.text: 그래, 예진이 너 왜 나한테 거짓말했어?
examples.trans: Yeah, Ye-jin, why did you lie to me?

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 거짓말하다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (lied).

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Used as concessive -아도 (골라도).

examples.text: 골라도 비싼 애기를 골랐어! 이 치사한 놈 진짜, 이거 손만 대봐!
examples.trans: Out of all of them, he picked an expensive baby! You petty jerk—just dare lay a finger on it!
Let us do that (even in picking) right away.

meanings.note: Softens a statement or downplays a motive.

examples.trans: I just asked out of curiosity.
I'll just stay home today.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

나가다.gloss: to go out, to step outside

meanings.en: to go out, to step outside, to leave a room
meanings.note: 나- ('out') + 가다 ('to go')

examples.trans: Let's step outside for a moment and talk.
He went out of the conference room.

meanings.en: to appear, be published, be achieved (a score/result)
meanings.note: Used for ratings, test scores, or results coming out

examples.trans: I came outside from the house.
The exam results came out well.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 술 많이 마신 날엔 밀가루 안 먹는다고 했는데 삼선짜장을 시키셔서, 어제 생각보다 많이 마신 건 아니지 않을까요?
examples.trans: He once said he avoids flour after heavy drinking yet ordered black-bean noodles—might he have drunk less than we thought?
Here the word for 'on days when' is key.
This is my bag.
My younger sibling is a student.

meanings.note: Contraction of 나 (I) + 의 (possessive)
Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 잘 가라, 준모는 성질 내놓고도 맘 약해서 십오 초 만에 후회할 거면서.
examples.trans: Off you go—even when Joon-mo loses his temper, he is too soft-hearted and regrets it within fifteen seconds anyway.
This expression comes from 'even after letting out'.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.trans: That is why you are a cruel jerk, do you know that?
Here the word for 'guy, jerk' is key.

meanings.note: Used as casual imperative (대봐!).

examples.text: 골라도 비싼 애기를 골랐어! 이 치사한 놈 진짜, 이거 손만 대봐!
examples.trans: Out of all of them, he picked an expensive baby! You petty jerk—just dare lay a finger on it!
Let us do that (just dare touch) right away.

examples.text: 조금만 더 가면 금방 도착할 것 같습니다.
examples.trans: If we go just a little farther, we should arrive soon.

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 도착하다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (will arrive).

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.
Please come into the room.

examples.text: 올해 우리 회사에 신입사원이 많이 들어왔어요.
examples.trans: Many new employees joined our company this year.

meanings.note: Compound of 들다 (enter) + 오다 (come)

meanings.en: to join (a company, school, or group)

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.

examples.trans: See you again!
It is raining again.

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 만약에 기억을 하는데도 아무 반응을 안 보이고 있는 거라면, 준모가 그 진심을 편집해버렸단 얘기 아닐까?
examples.trans: If he remembers everything and still shows no reaction, does that not mean Joon-mo edited out those feelings?
Here the word for 'if by chance' is key.

meanings.note: Auxiliary verb used after -지 to tell someone not to do something. Ending with -고 (말고) gives a brisk, trailing command. RR: malda.

examples.trans: Please do not worry.
Do not be late, and come early.

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.text: 어제는 너무 피곤해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.trans: I was so tired yesterday that I couldn't sleep.
Because it rained, we couldn't go on the picnic.

meanings.note: Used as nominalized -기 + object (무사하길).

examples.text: 이 가방이 무사하길 바란다면 30분 내로 집에 들어와라.
examples.trans: If you want this handbag to stay unharmed, get inside the house within thirty minutes.
It is really to remain safe compared to what I expected.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?
Is something the matter?

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.en: to be sorry; to feel apologetic
meanings.note: Descriptive adjective; used with peers or younger people (whereas 죄송하다 is honorific/humble).

examples.trans: I'm really sorry I'm late.

examples.text: 미안하지만 다시 한 번 말씀해 주세요.
examples.trans: I'm sorry, but please say that one more time.
I want to worth hoping for right now.
How about trying to worth hoping for together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Used as adnominal (비싼).

examples.text: 골라도 비싼 애기를 골랐어! 이 치사한 놈 진짜, 이거 손만 대봐!
examples.trans: Out of all of them, he picked an expensive baby! You petty jerk—just dare lay a finger on it!

examples.text: 생각해봐라, 행정반 월급으로 어떻게 그렇게 비싼 걸 입냐고! 이건 고위층과 모종의 관계가 있지 않고서야…
examples.trans: Think about it—how can she wear clothes that pricey on an admin salary? Unless she has secret ties to the brass…

meanings.note: adverbial form of 빠르다 (to be fast)

examples.trans: Please get ready quickly.
Time goes by so fast.

meanings.note: Used as verb + -잖아 (사과하잖아.).

examples.text: 아까도 미안했고 지난번에 내가 너한테 거짓말한 것도 미안했다고. 내가 사과하잖아.
examples.trans: I was sorry earlier and I am sorry for lying to you last time too—I am apologizing right here.
Let us do that (am apologizing, you see) right away.

meanings.note: in expressions like 뭔 소리야? ('what are you talking about?')
audible sound made by people or things

examples.trans: Suddenly a strange sound was heard.

examples.text: 말도 안 되는 소리 하지 마.
examples.trans: Don't talk nonsense.
Wash your hands.
Raise your right hand.

meanings.note: Available time or duration.
Used with native Korean numbers to count hours (한 시간 = one hour).

examples.trans: Do you have time?
It takes two hours.

meanings.en: earlier, a short while ago (same day)

examples.trans: I called earlier.
What did you say earlier?

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 암튼 내가 그날도 말했지만 공영방송에선 곤란해, 그런 옷.
examples.trans: Anyway, as I said that day too, an outfit like that is trouble on public television.
Here the word for 'anyway' is key.

meanings.note: Used as colloquial noun + dative (애기한테).

examples.text: 어머 어머, 이거 뭐야? 가위? 얘가 지금 우리 애기한테 무슨 짓을 하는 거지?
examples.trans: Oh my goodness, what is this—scissors? What is he doing to my baby right now?

examples.text: 골라도 비싼 애기를 골랐어! 이 치사한 놈 진짜, 이거 손만 대봐!
examples.trans: Out of all of them, he picked an expensive baby! You petty jerk—just dare lay a finger on it!

meanings.note: Casual exclamation used to call someone younger or a close friend.

examples.trans: Hey, come quickly!
Hey, where are you going?
This is my friend Minsu.
He/she did it all.

meanings.note: Contraction of 이 아이; used when introducing or referring to someone younger or close
Used as contracted casual question (어딨어?).

examples.trans: Where is my handbag?

examples.text: 글쎄 그게 무슨 또라이 같은 소리냐고! 박 군은 어딨니?
examples.trans: What kind of lunatic excuse is that?! Where is Manager Park?

meanings.note: Exclamation of surprise or realization.

examples.trans: Oh my, so nice to meet you!
Oh my, I left my phone behind.

meanings.note: Often used directly without a locative particle to mean 'here'.

examples.trans: Please sit here.
Here is our office.

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.

meanings.note: Used as noun + -도 (웃음도).

examples.text: 야, 너 초딩이냐? 유치해서 웃음도 안 나와.
examples.trans: Hey, are you a grade-schooler? That is so childish I cannot even laugh.
This point about even a laugh is really important.

meanings.note: Used as causal -어서 (유치해서).

examples.text: 야, 너 초딩이냐? 유치해서 웃음도 안 나와.
examples.trans: Hey, are you a grade-schooler? That is so childish I cannot even laugh.
It is really because it is childish compared to what I expected.

meanings.note: demonstrative determiner placed before a noun

examples.text: 이 바닥은 자기 밥그릇은 자기가 챙겨야 돼.
examples.trans: In this industry, you have to look after your own rice bowl.
This book is interesting.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken contraction of 이것.

examples.trans: How much is this?
Please look at this.

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

We decided at the last meeting.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?
I'm on my way home right now.
On weekends I usually rest at home.

meanings.note: Used as noun + object (짓을).

examples.text: 어머 어머, 이거 뭐야? 가위? 얘가 지금 우리 애기한테 무슨 짓을 하는 거지?

examples.trans: If you fail to arrive in time, even I cannot guarantee what I might do to this little one.

meanings.note: Used as slang noun + plain question (초딩이냐?).

examples.text: 야, 너 초딩이냐? 유치해서 웃음도 안 나와.
examples.trans: Hey, are you a grade-schooler? That is so childish I cannot even laugh.
This point about are you a grade-schooler is really important.

meanings.note: Used as adnominal (치사한).

examples.text: 골라도 비싼 애기를 골랐어! 이 치사한 놈 진짜, 이거 손만 대봐!
examples.trans: Out of all of them, he picked an expensive baby! You petty jerk—just dare lay a finger on it!
It is really petty, underhanded compared to what I expected.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.
